newsitem.title: JAPAN: Jump in Japan car exports to U.S. unlikely -- Nissan.
newsitem.headline: Jump in Japan car exports to U.S. unlikely -- Nissan.

text.p: Japanese car exports to the United States are unlikely to increase as much this year as in 1996 because if they did so it could cause trade friction, Nissan Motor Co Ltd president Yoshikazu Hanawa said on Wednesday.
"We have had experience (with trade friction in the past) and learned a lot, so the Japanese car industry is unlikely to boost exports to the United States sharply," Hanawa told a news conference.
Last week, Japan's Trade Minister Shinji Sato urged automotive industry leaders to carefully moderate their exports.

On Monday, Japan announced that its trade surplus had risen 6.5 percent in February from the same month a year earlier to 686.72 billion yen, the first increase since November 1994, and that the sensitive trade surplus with the United States -- which has voiced concern recently about a possible increase in the surplus -- grew by 12.3 percent to 407.35 billion yen, due to higher exports of cars and computers.
Japan's vehicle exports to the United States rose 75.3 percent to 124,834 in January, marking the fifth successive month they have gained on a year-on-year basis.
